# v4.1.3 No more phantom ENG keyboard layout

## Summary

- Fixed the helper adding a phantom `ENG / English (United States)` entry to the system input-method list on startup (#10). Every previous build called `LoadKeyboardLayoutW("00000409", KLF_ACTIVATE)` unconditionally at launch; `LoadKeyboardLayoutW` registers the layout with the **system** input list and `KLF_ACTIVATE` activates it immediately, so `Win + Space` gained an `ENG` entry — and the taskbar IME indicator reappeared — even for users who never added English to their language list
- No keyboard-layout work happens at startup any more. The English layout is resolved lazily, only inside the compatibility-mode paste path, and only when the selected strategy actually needs it
- New `ime_protection` setting (tray submenu `输入法保护` + `wsl_clipboard.toml`) with four strictly increasing levels:
  - `off` — never touches the IME
  - `imm` (new default) — closes only the foreground window's IME open status via `ImmGetDefaultIMEWnd` + `WM_IME_CONTROL`/`IMC_SETOPENSTATUS`, restoring it after the paste; **never** touches keyboard layouts, so it cannot pollute the input-method list
  - `layout` — switches to an English layout but **only reuses** one already installed (discovered with `GetKeyboardLayoutList`); skips the switch when none exists
  - `layout-force` — legacy-strength behaviour: loads `ENG` on demand **without** `KLF_ACTIVATE`, passes `KLF_NOTELLSHELL` so the shell/taskbar indicator is not woken up, and calls `UnloadKeyboardLayout` on exit
- IME calls now use `SendMessageTimeoutW` with `SMTO_ABORTIFHUNG` and an 80 ms timeout, so an unresponsive foreground window can no longer stall the paste path
- Existing `wsl_clipboard.toml` files keep working unchanged: the new field is optional and defaults to `imm`

## Upgrade note

If an earlier version already left English (United States) in your Windows language list, remove it once under
`Settings → Time & language → Language & region`. This build will not add it back.

## Known follow-up

`scripts/wsl_clipboard.ahk` (legacy v3 AutoHotkey build) still contains the original
`LoadKeyboardLayoutW(..., KLF_ACTIVATE)` startup preload and is unaffected by this fix.
